content: this is a summary of a civil case that took place in the alytus district court the case involved a plaintiff and an unidentified second party the final resolution of the case was the division of matrimonial property specifically immovable property the marriage between the plaintiff and the defendant has been dissolved both parties are responsible for fulfilling any outstanding obligations to a creditor the plaintiff will personally fulfill their obligations and can claim reimbursement from the defendant for their share of the discharged obligations the plaintiff has acquired a 50 ownership right to a land plot the property will be divided between the spouses with the remaining portion being the defendants personal property the plaintiff is seeking the dissolution of their marriage due to faults on both sides and wants to retain their surname they also want to personally fulfill the obligations of a consumer credit agreement while both parties will remain jointly and severally liable towards another creditor the plaintiff claims that they have been separated from the defendant for 6 years and that the defendants heavy drinking has caused problems the defendant suffered a stroke and is in a care home the plaintiff is asking the court to dissolve the marriage and is also claiming maintenance from the defendant the couple has minor children and property that needs to be divided the defendant has filed a statement of defense and the creditor has objected to the claim for debt repayment the court has allowed the action to proceed and has determined that the division of property must be resolved as part of the dissolution of the marriage the court has clarified the liability of spouses towards creditors the plaintiff is personally responsible for a consumer credit agreement and both parties are jointly and severally liable to another creditor the court will also decide on the allocation of costs in the case the court has allowed the full dissolution of the marriage declaring it to be the fault of both spouses the plaintiff is responsible for fulfilling their obligations towards one creditor while both parties are jointly and severally liable towards another creditor
